items.title: 3 Utility Dividend Stocks Built to Keep Paying in Any Economy
items.summary: Not every dividend stock survives a recession with its payout intact, but regulated utilities operate under a different set of rules entirely. These three have raised dividends for decades by design, and the mechanics behind that streak are worth understanding before the next downturn tests your portfolio.

items.title: My mother, 91, has dementia. Every bank says I need her signature to unlock her $100,000 stock certificate. What can I do?
items.summary: “These shares are the only assets in her estate without designated beneficiaries.”

items.title: 5 Dividend Aristocrats That Belong in Every Income Portfolio
items.summary: Not every Dividend Aristocrat deserves space in your portfolio right now, and with tariffs, rate pressure, and AI capex reshaping entire industries, picking the wrong ones could cost you real income. These five names survived a brutal four-factor ranking, but only one scored clean across the board.

items.title: How a Negative Beta Bet Can Protect Your Portfolio From an AI Selloff
items.summary: AI is shaking up a lot of things—including which stocks investors can expect to hold up in a market selloff.  Investors have long relied on a mathematical measure known as beta to judge market risk.  A stock with a beta of 1 tends to move in line with the stock market.

items.title: Can Consolidated Edison (ED) Still Trade At A Discount?
items.summary: Consolidated Edison stock has delivered a 64.1% total return over the past 5 years, and today the Dividend Discount Model (DDM) intrinsic value estimate sits very close to the current share price, while earnings-based multiples still screen the stock as somewhat undervalued. That mix, along with a mid-range valuation score, suggests the share price may be roughly in line with intrinsic value but without a clear margin of safety.
